metadata.note: The Bellefonte Central Railroad -- a short line built for iron ore, limestone, and lumber that ended up best remembered for carrying Penn State students home for the holidays. Its predecessor, the Buffalo Run, Bellefonte and Bald Eagle Railroad (BRB&BE), opened in 1886 hauling ore from deposits near Struble to Bellefonte. Foreclosed in 1891, it was reorganized May 9 1892 as the Bellefonte Central (BFC), which built a new branch from a wye at Struble into State College -- turning a freight tramway into a passenger link between Pennsylvania State College and the outside world, connecting at Bellefonte to the Pennsylvania Railroad. The ~19-20 mile route followed Spring Creek and Buffalo Run through Fillmore and Waddle. Students nicknamed the train 'Parker's Boat' after longtime conductor G. Ross Parker; the ride grew notoriously slow as freight cars were added, sometimes walking pace, with passengers occasionally hopping off to pick flowers or wait out livestock on the tracks. Automobiles and buses eroded ridership after about 1920, and by 1946 passenger runs were 'special occasion' only (a notable one carried Dwight Eisenhower to campus in 1953). Coal-to-Penn-State traffic (the railroad's last major freight business) switched to trucks in 1959; Hurricane Agnes wrecked the line in 1972, and it was formally abandoned in 1984. GEOMETRY METHODOLOGY: real-traced through OpenStreetMap active/abandoned-rail data (Overpass API, shortest-path graph search) for the Bellefonte-to-near-Waddle portion, with a short hand-placed segment into State College itself where Overpass found no further connected trackage (consistent with the 1972 Hurricane Agnes damage and subsequent track removal). Traced length 19.2 km / 11.9 mi comes in shorter than the sourced ~19-20 mile route -- likely because the surviving/mapped remnant no longer preserves the original line's full curves.
